problem: Find an upper bound for $T(n)=T(\sqrt{n})+10\log\log n$
proof_numbered:
0001 | I need to find an upper bound for $T(n)=T(\sqrt{n})+10\log\log n$.
0002 | 
0003 | I thought first to make a substitution: $m=\log n$. Then:
0004 | $$
0005 | T(2^m)=T(2^{m \over 2})+10\log m
0006 | $$
0007 | Let $S(m)=T(2^m)$:
0008 | $$
0009 | S(m)=S\big({m \over 2}\big)+10\log m
0010 | $$
0011 | 
0012 | Now we can use Master theorem. 
0013 | 
0014 | Suppose it's the case when $f(m)=O(m^{\log_2 1-\epsilon})=O(m^{0-\epsilon})$. Let $\epsilon=0.5$ then:
0015 | $$
0016 | \lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{10\log m}{m^{0.5}}=0
0017 | $$
0018 | Hence according to the Master theorem $T(m)=\Theta(m^0)=\Theta(1)$.
0019 | 
0020 | Am I in the right direction?
